key_insight: DFT predicts that certain shear strains transform monolayer hexagonal boron nitride into an ordered orthorhombic pmmm phase with a narrow band gap of approximately 0.65 eV.
engineering_relevance: Strain-induced phase transformation could enable band-gap engineering of monolayer boron nitride from a wide-gap insulator toward a narrow-gap semiconductor.
method: First-principles DFT using pseudopotentials and PBE exchange–correlation.
Structural and electronic analysis under different strain types and directions.
First-principles Born–Oppenheimer molecular dynamics for thermal stability.
evidence_signal: Simulations predict an orthorhombic phase under certain shear strains, demonstrate thermal stability up to approximately 900 K, and estimate its band gap at approximately 0.65 eV.
watch_item: Experimental realization remains unverified, and the transformation occurs under strong deformation associated with elastic failure.
paper_title: Strain-induced structural transformations in hexagonal monolayer boron nitride. A density functional study
